reason: The text contradicts this statement. While Yahweh does make specific promises to Abram (the leader), the passage explicitly extends blessings beyond him to all humanity. The crucial phrase states 'וְנִבְרְכ֣וּ בְךָ֔ כֹּ֖ל מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הָאֲדָמָֽה' ('all families of the earth shall be blessed [in/through you]'). This demonstrates that Yahweh's care extends through the leader to encompass all people, not merely the leader at the expense of the people. The blessings flow from Abram to humanity universally.
